reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports improved corrosion resistance in a room-temperature NaCl solution, but the hypothesis relies on high-temperature oxidation/corrosion resistance and specific mechanisms (oxygen barrier, grain boundary pinning) that are not addressed by E1. The key premises about high-temperature behavior and the dispersoid mechanism lack direct prior evidence.
premises: ZrC addition improves corrosion resistance of CrMnFeCoNi HEA coating
Corrosion resistance increases with ZrC content
Annual corrosion rate of 4 wt% ZrC coating is 21.5% of unmodified HEA in NaCl solution
ZrC forms a stable dispersoid phase that retards oxidation and corrosion at high temperatures
ZrC particles act as barriers against oxygen diffusion and grain boundary pinning sites
